workflow: wf_fe9e9434-59c (ga-design-exploration; 5 substrate maps -> 4 approaches -> judge synthesis; 10 agents)
note: G(a) obligation-coverage design exploration. Recommended = Obligation-Coverage Ratchet (9/10).

scored_approaches.name: Runtime asserted_obligation_ids + per-validator coverage gate (M1-trio first slice)
scored_approaches.verdict: Sound dynamic substrate, correct hash-safety reasoning, but its scope-bounding lever (an INSTRUMENTED_VALIDATORS allowlist in code) is weaker than a checked-in ledger: the 'declared-but-uncovered' set is implicit (everything-not-in-allowlist) and not a visible, diffable, ratcheted artifact, so it does not make the backlog monotonically shrink as a first-class gate condition.

scored_approaches.name: Coverage-by-Execution: assertObligation() recorder + harvest existing unit tests + set-difference gate
scored_approaches.verdict: Strongest substrate design: the assertObligation() helper centralizes the recording concept (one deletion boundary), block-TOP placement gives true PASS/FAIL-independence, and harvesting off the EXISTING 31 reconstruct *.test.ts avoids building a dispatcher/fixture that rots. Honest about rubber-stamp and fixture-path limits. Loses a point only because, like #1, its in-scope set is code-declared rather than a visible ratcheted ledger — the backlog is real but not enforced-to-shrink.

scored_approaches.name: Tested-Enforcer Binding Registry (obligation_id -> {validator_id, enforcerHandle, redLineTest})
scored_approaches.verdict: Uniquely proves the enforcer REJECTS bad input (red-line negative test), strictly stronger on the 'is the enforcer real' axis than a reached-control token. But it re-introduces a curated obligation_id->enforcer binding STRING — the exact 'static map = declared-only' pattern the design rejected — now backstopped by 'fn rejects SOME input', and shared violation codes (missing_required_coverage fires for two sibling obligations at maturation-validation.ts:824-837 and :885) make 'the RIGHT obligation fired' unprovable without fragile subject_id matching. The ~248 unenforced active obligations become a large allowlist escape hatch with no ratchet.

scored_approaches.name: Obligation-Coverage Ratchet (asserted_obligation_ids + monotone-shrink pending tier)
scored_approaches.verdict: Best fit to the explicit decision criterion: makes 'declared-but-uncovered' a VISIBLE checked-in ledger (.onto/.../obligation-coverage-ledger.yaml) and a RATCHET (pending may not grow vs origin/main, may not re-park a recorded id) guarantees monotone shrink without forcing 297 at once. Inherits #2's correct dynamic recording substrate, the verified hash-safety of the M1 artifacts (off the authoredArtifactReuseMatch five), and reuses the failure vocabulary verbatim. Honest about its core limit (records reached-control, not semantic correctness). The ratchet predicate is the one subtle thing to get exactly right.

recommended_approach: Hybrid: Approach 4 (Obligation-Coverage Ratchet) as the spine — visible checked-in pending ledger + monotone ratchet — recording the obligation ids via Approach 2's centralized assertObligation(acc, id) helper placed at block-TOP and harvested from the EXISTING reconstruct *.test.ts fixtures (no new dispatcher). Borrow Approach 3's red-line negative-input assertion as a per-obligation TEST EXPECTATION (not as the gate's binding mechanism) to narrow the rubber-stamp hole for the first slice only.
rationale: The prompt's decisive instruction is to favor an approach that makes 'declared-but-uncovered' VISIBLE and monotonically shrinking over one that covers 297 at once. Only Approach 4 turns the backlog into a first-class, diffable, ratcheted artifact; Approaches 1 and 2 keep the in-scope set implicit in code (everything-not-in-allowlist), which is correct but invisible and not enforced-to-shrink. I verified the load-bearing substrate against the real code: (1) the recording field is genuinely unbuilt — grep asserted_obligation in src/ scripts/ = 0 hits, so this is ADD-substrate work, not a static map (which the design rejects at 20260619-...-design.md:73-78). (2) The M1 trio is hash-safe for the first slice: the reuse hash hazard is real and narrow — reuseMatchArtifactHash (run.ts:1078-1080) strips ONLY created_at/emitted_at (stripVolatileArtifactFields run.ts:1059-1076), and the FIVE hashed validation artifacts are exactly targetMaterialProfileValidation/sourceSafetyLedgerValidation/sourceScoutPackValidation/sourceObservationLineageIndexValidation/seedAuthoringReadinessValidation (run.ts:1167/1193/1199/1202/1206); the maturation-baseline and actionability-matrix validation artifacts are NOT in authoredArtifactReuseMatch's signature, so adding a field to them rotates nothing. (3) The registry side is already hash-neutral via the projectValidatorRecordSnapshotFields ALLOW-LIST (governing-snapshot.ts:446-459) added by #108, and obligations are preserved on ReconstructValidatorRecord (contract-registry.ts:146-147, parsed via optionalStringArray + parseConditionalValidationObligation at 725-747). (4) The M1 enforcer block is a real, recordable check-unit: validateMaturationBaseline's coverage block (maturation-validation.ts:868-903) emits missing_required_coverage/conflicting_state and is the live enforcer for validate_baseline_rows_cover_selected_purpose_frame_required_elements; validateActionabilityMatrix's id/ref blocks (1278-1320) enforce validate_matrix_row_ids_are_stable_and_baseline_row_refs_close. (5) The gate skeleton and registration are pure reuse: clone scripts/check-final-output-sections-parity.ts (pure evaluate()->string[] + thin main + direct-invoke guard), add a GUARDS[] row to check-invariant-drift.ts:30-73, add check:obligation-coverage to package.json (51-53 pattern). I picked Approach 2's centralized assertObligation() helper over inline pushes (Approach 4's literal push) because it gives ONE deletion boundary and forces block-TOP, pass/fail-independent placement — without it, a push placed inside an `if (violation)` branch would falsely read clean runs as uncovered. I demote Approach 3 from the spine because its binding STRING re-creates the declared-only pattern and shared violation codes (missing_required_coverage fires for two sibling baseline obligations) make per-obligation attribution fragile; but its red-line negative test is the only thing that touches the rubber-stamp hole, so I keep it as a per-obligation test expectation in the first slice. Net: this proves WIRED-ness dynamically and makes the gap monotonically shrink; it does NOT prove the enforcer is semantically CORRECT — that residual (R5's 구조증명 불가) is named, not hidden.

design_skeleton.goal: Make the repo's canonical 'declared validation_obligation with no live enforcer' a BUILD ERROR, not a review round: every ACTIVE registry obligation must be either dynamically proven-asserted on its own validator path (recorded asserted_obligation_ids harvested from real validator execution) OR explicitly parked in a checked-in pending ledger that can only ever shrink — so the uncovered set is VISIBLE and monotonically shrinking, never a 297-line big-bang.
design_skeleton.scope: IN SCOPE: (1) a new asserted_obligation_ids: string[] field on the in-scope Reconstruct*ValidationArtifact interfaces (artifact-types.ts), starting with ReconstructMaturationBaselineValidationArtifact (:1960-1975) and ReconstructActionabilityMatrixValidationArtifact (:2015-2029). (2) a centralized assertObligation(acc, id) recorder helper (one small module, the deletion boundary) called at block-TOP inside the M1 validate* bodies (maturation-validation.ts:872 coverage block, :1278 id/ref blocks), returned in the artifact literal at :904-925 next to validation_results. (3) a checked-in pending ledger .onto/processes/reconstruct/obligation-coverage-ledger.yaml listing every ACTIVE (validator_id, obligation_id) NOT yet recorded, coverage_status: pending. (4) scripts/check-obligation-coverage.ts (clone of check-final-output-sections-parity.ts) with a pure evaluateObligationCoverage()->string[], a harvest that re-runs the existing maturation-validation.test.ts validators and reads back asserted_obligation_ids, and the RATCHET. (5) check:obligation-coverage npm script + one GUARDS[] row in check-invariant-drift.ts. (6) one new INV (INV-OBLIGATION-COVERAGE-1) in INVARIANTS.md with an INVARIANT-CHANGE marker. OUT OF SCOPE: instrumenting the other ~37 active validators (each later PR shrinks the ledger); the 5 conditional obligations stay tier-tagged-but-exempt until their activation_condition predicate is implemented; planned_validator_records stays report-only; semantic-correctness proof of enforcers (rubber-stamp residual is named, not closed); NO new obligation concepts (G(a) wires the 297 already declared).
design_skeleton.architecture: THREE LAYERS keyed on (validator_id, obligation_id) — never global obligation_id (verified: 7 strings recur across validators, e.g. reject_actionable_ready... at registry :2752/:2774/:2811). LAYER 1 RECORDING (runtime, per-validator): assertObligation(acc, id) pushes the obligation id when control reaches the authored check-BLOCK, pass/fail-independent; emitted as asserted_obligation_ids on the validation artifact. The field is a validation OUTPUT, off the validator_records snapshot family, and (for the M1 trio) off the authoredArtifactReuseMatch five — so it rotates NO reuse hash. LAYER 2 HARVEST (CI): the gate imports the in-scope validate* and reads asserted_obligation_ids off the artifacts the EXISTING maturation-validation.test.ts fixtures already produce (validateMaturationBaseline, validateActionabilityMatrix called directly there) — the field is the truth; the harness only reads it back, mirroring registry-verification-validation.ts:244-289's expected-vs-actual listDelta. NO new validator dispatcher is built. LAYER 3 GATE+RATCHET: evaluateObligationCoverage() loads EXPECTED active obligations via loadReconstructContractRegistry (validation_obligations preserved at contract-registry.ts:146; conditional overlay JOINed by obligation_id, tier-tagged, exempt until predicate live; planned_validator_records read via raw-YAML walk, report-only), reads the harvested asserted set and the pending ledger, then fails CI on: (a) an ACTIVE obligation that is NEITHER recorded NOR in the ledger (anti-fooling completeness, mirrors G9 item-6 'a 9th section fails CI'); (b) a recorded id that maps to no current active registry obligation for that validator (reverse-validation per onto issue-001, code conflicting_state/registry_claim_mismatch, reused verbatim from registry-verification-validation.ts:291); (c) the RATCHET — the ledger may not GROW vs origin/main except by genuinely newly-declared-active obligations, and may not contain any id already recorded (you cannot re-park a covered obligation). Registered as a net-new GUARDS[] row (check-invariant-drift.ts:30-73) mapped to a NEW INV-OBLIGATION-COVERAGE-1 (NOT INV-SCHEMA-1, which is schema-shape; this is enforcement-coverage). Reuses failure vocabulary verbatim (missing_required_coverage/duplicate_id/conflicting_state already a closed union at artifact-types.ts:1938-1955); net-new obligation concepts = 0.
design_skeleton.first_slice: ONE PR, ~19-id blast radius, fully GREEN on merge (the rest parked in the ledger). Steps: (1) add assertObligation(acc, id) helper module (deletion boundary). (2) add asserted_obligation_ids: string[] to ReconstructMaturationBaselineValidationArtifact (artifact-types.ts:1960) and ReconstructActionabilityMatrixValidationArtifact (:2015) — both MATURATION-stage, CONFIRMED absent from the authoredArtifactReuseMatch five (run.ts:1167/1193/1199/1202/1206), so NO stripVolatileArtifactFields change. (3) call assertObligation at the M1 coverage block top (maturation-validation.ts:872, before the if(selected) predicate) recording validate_baseline_rows_cover_selected_purpose_frame_required_elements, and at the matrix id/ref blocks (:1278) recording validate_matrix_row_ids_are_stable_and_baseline_row_refs_close — record ONLY the obligations M1 genuinely asserts; do NOT over-claim the sibling obligations whose block does not yet exist (those go to the ledger). (4) seed obligation-coverage-ledger.yaml with every OTHER active (validator_id, obligation_id) as coverage_status: pending. (5) add scripts/check-obligation-coverage.ts (clone check-final-output-sections-parity.ts) with evaluateObligationCoverage() + co-located self-test + the ratchet. (6) add a harvest assertion in maturation-validation.test.ts (asserts the two validators return the expected asserted_obligation_ids). (7) register check:obligation-coverage (package.json) + a GUARDS[] row (check-invariant-drift.ts). (8) add INV-OBLIGATION-COVERAGE-1 to INVARIANTS.md with the INVARIANT-CHANGE marker (touches G4-protected surface). VERIFY: full vitest + check:ts-core + the new guard green; flip-test (delete the flagship assertObligation call -> guard RED); negative-input red-line test (a violating baseline -> missing_required_coverage AND the id recorded, narrowing rubber-stamp for these two); add an unenforced active obligation to the YAML not in the ledger -> guard RED; governing-snapshot.test + reuse-provenance tests byte-identical (proving the new field rotates no reuse hash). Each later PR moves ids pending->recorded; the ratchet forbids regression.
success_criteria: A NEW active obligation added to the registry YAML with neither a recorded assertion nor a pending-ledger entry FAILS check:obligation-coverage in CI (proven by a deliberate add-and-expect-red test in the guard's self-test).

Deleting the flagship assertObligation call from the M1 coverage block (maturation-validation.ts:872) FLIPS the guard RED — proving the proof is dynamic (recorded from real execution), not a static declared-only map.

The pending ledger is monotone: the ratchet rejects any PR whose ledger GROWS vs origin/main (except by newly-declared-active obligations) or RE-PARKS an already-recorded id — verified by a self-test feeding a grown ledger.

The new asserted_obligation_ids field rotates NO reuse hash: governing-snapshot.test and the reuse-provenance/reuse_match_hash tests are byte-identical to main (the M1 trio is off the authoredArtifactReuseMatch five and off the validator_records snapshot allow-list).

Coverage is keyed on (validator_id, obligation_id): a unit test proves one validator's recorded id cannot 'cover' the same obligation string declared on a different validator (the 7 cross-validator duplicates), and that the 5 conditional ids are JOINed (not double-counted) and exempt until their activation_condition predicate is implemented.

Reverse-validation works: a recorded asserted id that no longer maps to a current active registry obligation for its validator FAILS the guard (conflicting_state/registry_claim_mismatch), catching a rename/typo on either side.

Concept economy holds: net-new = exactly one field (asserted_obligation_ids), one recorder helper, one ledger artifact, one guard script, one INV; zero new obligation concepts and zero new failure codes (all reused from artifact-types.ts:1938-1955).

open_questions: INV identity: confirm a NEW INV-OBLIGATION-COVERAGE-1 (enforcement-coverage) vs overloading INV-SCHEMA-1 (schema-shape, used by G8/G9). A new INV needs an INVARIANT-CHANGE marker and touches the G4-protected INVARIANTS.md/invariants.yml surface — owner must approve the marker and the exact INV id (handoff already flags INV-REGISTRY-PARITY-1 as an alternative name).

Ratchet predicate exactness: define precisely when the pending ledger is ALLOWED to grow. 'Never grow' blocks legitimately adding a new active obligation to the YAML; 'grow only by newly-declared-active obligations' is correct but requires the gate to diff the registry's active obligation set vs origin/main too. Owner must decide whether the gate computes the newly-declared set from the registry diff or trusts an explicit per-entry justification field in the ledger.

Rubber-stamp residual policy: assertObligation records 'control reached a labeled block', NOT 'the block semantically enforces the obligation'. For the M1 trio the red-line negative test narrows this, but the project-wide policy (does every later validator's instrumentation REQUIRE a paired negative-input test, or is reached-control sufficient?) must be set by the owner — it materially changes per-validator authoring cost.

Zero-obligation active validators: confirm the current state (source-frontier, source-observation-directive, seed-confirmation, revision-proposal carry zero obligations and are vacuously covered) is INTENDED, or whether the gate should flag an active validator with a gate_id but zero declared obligations as under-declared. The substrate allows either (loader defaults to []).

Pending-wall permanence: the ratchet guarantees non-increase but does NOT force the ~248 pending set toward zero on any schedule. Owner must decide whether that is acceptable (gate proves 'no NEW silent gaps' + visible backlog) or whether a separate burn-down target/owner is assigned, so the gate's value posture is explicit.

Harvest source coupling: the first slice harvests asserted_obligation_ids by reusing maturation-validation.test.ts. Owner must confirm the harvest reads back the field from the EXISTING test fixtures (not a bespoke re-staged fixture), and decide the policy for an obligation whose block is only reachable under an input shape no current test drives (treat as a coverage hole to fix by adding a fixture, never by suppressing).

SSOT for the id strings: obligation ids are opaque free-form prose with no namespace; a matched-pair rename on both the YAML and the inline string literal passes the bidirectional check while silently mis-binding. Owner should decide whether to generate a TS const from the registry YAML so both the recorder and the gate cite ONE symbol, vs accepting inline string literals with the reverse-validation as the only guard.

obligation-data: Coverage key MUST be (validator_id, obligation_id), NOT a global obligation_id — 7 obligation strings recur across validators (10 occurrences), so a global set would let an enforcer 'cover' an obligation on a path where it was never asserted.

The gate MUST read obligations from TWO places per validator: .validation_obligations (flat string[]) and .conditional_validation_obligations[].obligation_id. The 5 conditional ids are an ACTIVATION OVERLAY that ALSO appear in the same validator's flat list — join by obligation_id, do not double-count, and use the overlay to assign 'conditional/activation-gated' tier.

Three tiers come from STRUCTURE, not id-parsing: validator_records.flat = mandatory-active; conditional_validation_obligations = active-but-activation-gated (mandatory once predicate implemented); planned_validator_records.flat = planned-coverage status (not forced active). Tier is determined by which YAML section/array the obligation lives in.

The gate MUST tolerate empty obligation arrays: 4 active validators (source-frontier, source-observation-directive, seed-confirmation, revision-proposal) declare ZERO obligations. The loader already defaults these to [] (optionalStringArray / conditional default). Decide explicitly whether zero-obligation active validators are allowed (current state) or reported as under-declared.

Obligation ids are opaque free-form prose strings with no namespace/schema/version — intent cannot be parsed from the id. Coverage MUST be string set-difference between a registry-derived id list and an enforcer-recorded id list (asserted_obligation_ids), and both sides MUST reference ONE SSOT id list or a rename/typo silently breaks coverage.

asserted_obligation_ids does not exist and NO obligation id is referenced in src/ today — even the M1 'named enforcers' do not record the ids they assert. G(a) must ADD the recording substrate (per design, on the 41 *ValidationArtifact interfaces in artifact-types.ts) before any coverage check is non-vacuous; a static obligation_id->handle map is explicitly rejected as 'declared-only'.

The loader must surface planned_validator_records (separate top-level key) to the gate; contract-registry.ts currently parses only validator_records into ReconstructValidatorRecord[]. Either extend the loader or have the gate walk raw YAML for the planned tier.

Instrumentation is incremental-friendly: obligation load is concentrated (~3 validators hold ~24% of active obligations; pre-handoff=27, competency-questions=23, ontology-seed=13). Start the gate on already-named enforcers (M1's maturation-baseline/baseline-actionability-matrix = 12 obligations) and report uncovered-but-active obligations as a known-gap list rather than blocking on all 267 at once.
obligation-to-code: Assertion semantics must be PASS/FAIL-independent: asserted_obligation_ids must record that a validator EXECUTED an obligation's check-unit, not that it emitted a violation — otherwise a clean (valid, violations=[]) run records zero assertions and the gate falsely reports every obligation unenforced. This rules out deriving coverage from the existing violations[] output.

The recordable unit is an author-placed instrumentation token per check-BLOCK (e.g. an assertObligation('id') accumulator), NOT a violation code: obligation->code is many:many (run-control 5 obligations vs 14 codes/22 pushes; maturation obligations share missing_required_coverage / conflicting_state across siblings), so no automatic code-value->obligation_id mapping is sound.

asserted_obligation_ids must be added to the per-validator validation artifact interfaces (artifact-types.ts ~48 Reconstruct*ValidationArtifact) and POPULATED inside each validator body — the substrate is type-addable but every validator function must be edited; it cannot be back-derived from validation_results (coarse single-element pass/fail) or from source text.

The gate must scope by tier exactly: validation_obligations (267 across 40 validators) = mandatory-active and each must have a recorded assertion on its validator path; conditional_validation_obligations (5) = mandatory only once the activation predicate is implemented; planned_validator_records (8) = a separate planned-coverage status, never forced active.

Zero-obligation active validators (source-frontier-validator, source-observation-directive-validator, seed-confirmation-validator, revision-proposal-validator) must be treated as vacuously covered, not as coverage holes.

Obligations declared on MULTIPLE validators (e.g. validate_matrix_row_ids_are_stable_and_baseline_row_refs_close on both baseline-actionability-matrix-validator and actionability-matrix-validator) require per-validator-path coverage: a recorded assertion must be attributed to the (validator_id, obligation_id) pair, not to the obligation_id globally.

The proof must be DYNAMIC (execute each validator path and capture invoked handles), not a static obligation_id->handle table and not a static source-text scan like G8/G9 — a static map is itself unverifiable 'declared-only' text, and obligation->code-block boundaries are not statically recoverable.

The gate registers as a net-new GuardRun in scripts/check-invariant-drift.ts mapped to INV-SCHEMA-1 (G8/G9 precedent), but every active (validator_id, obligation_id) pair lacking a recorded assertion on its driven path must be a CI FAILURE — the canonical 'declared validation_obligation with no live enforcer' becomes a build error.

registry-verification-validator's require_evidence_row_for_each_current_registry_subject_id loop (registry-verification-validation.ts:351-388, one block -> one code) is the canonical template for what a cleanly-recordable assertion looks like; G(a)'s instrumentation should target the same block-granularity that obligations were authored at.
artifact-substrate: A runtime `asserted_obligation_ids` field MUST NOT be added to any of the five source/seed-stage validation artifacts that feed `authoredArtifactReuseMatch` (targetMaterialProfileValidation, sourceSafetyLedgerValidation, sourceScoutPackValidation, sourceObservationLineageIndexValidation, seedAuthoringReadinessValidation — run.ts:1167/1193/1199/1202/1206) without ALSO excluding it from the hash, because `reuseMatchArtifactHash` (run.ts:1078) hashes the whole object minus only created_at/emitted_at. Either (a) place the field only on artifacts NOT in the reuse-match set (e.g. the maturation-stage enforcers, which are absent from the set), or (b) extend `stripVolatileArtifactFields` (run.ts:1059) to strip `asserted_obligation_ids` so it stays out of the reuse hash, with a regression test proving the five family shas are byte-identical to main.

`asserted_obligation_ids` is a PER-ARTIFACT field (one per `Reconstruct*ValidationArtifact` interface that records assertions), not a single shared object — the artifacts are distinct types with no common base. It must be populated inside the existing pure `validate*` body at the same point `violations`/`validation_status` are decided, so the recording cannot diverge from what production actually asserts (the design's 'dynamic proof, not declared-only map' requirement).

The recording site of truth must be the runtime field, not a standalone CI fixture: a fixture that re-stages and re-executes 48 validator paths is a second realization of the same call graph that rots independently. If a fixture/harness is used, it must READ BACK the runtime-written `asserted_obligation_ids`, mirroring the registry-verification validator's expected-vs-actual id-set delta pattern (registry-verification-validation.ts:244-289), not re-derive assertions on its own.

The loader/registry half is already reuse-hash-safe and must stay that way: `validation_obligations`/`conditional_validation_obligations` are preserved on `ReconstructValidatorRecord` (contract-registry.ts:146-147) but excluded from the snapshot via the `projectValidatorRecordSnapshotFields` allow-list (governing-snapshot.ts:446-459). G(a) must read obligations through the loader for the expected set and MUST NOT add obligations to the validator_records snapshot family.

Tier scoping is mandatory in the gate's expected-set construction: `validation_obligations` (40 blocks across 48 validators) = mandatory-active; `conditional_validation_obligations` (3 blocks, structured shape) = mandatory only once the activation predicate is implemented; `planned_validator_records` (1 section) = a separate planned-coverage status that is NOT forced active. Conflating these collapses the gate into an un-landable red wall given ~292 obligations have no enforcer yet.

The gate must be bidirectional (per the prior onto review issue-001 at .onto/review/20260619-fa98af28): fail when an active obligation has no recorded assertion AND fail when a recorded `asserted_obligation_ids` value is unknown/stale/duplicate/assigned to the wrong validator/not assertable under its current tier — recorded ids are now part of the coverage domain and can drift independently of the registry.
existing-coverage-machinery: G(a) MUST be DYNAMIC: a static obligation_id->handle table is rejected by the design as 'declared-only'. The gate must consume evidence that each ACTIVE obligation was actually asserted on its validator path (recorded asserted_obligation_ids OR a CI fixture that executes the validator and captures invoked handles). The static skeleton (registry-side structural checks) is reusable from G8/G9 but does NOT discharge the dynamic requirement.

The asserted_obligation_ids substrate does NOT exist and must be invented. The natural carrier is the uniform `validation_results: string[]` / a new sibling field on the per-stage *ValidationArtifact interfaces; recording must occur on BOTH valid and invalid runs (an invalid run must still prove the obligation was checked, else it reads as uncovered).

Obligation ids read for the coverage gate MUST NOT enter governing-snapshot / the reuse hash (governing-snapshot.ts:602-609 explicitly excludes them to keep the family sha byte-identical). G(a) is a CI-time static+fixture gate, not a runtime snapshot/reuse-hash field.

Tier scoping is mandatory and the registry already encodes it: validator_records.validation_obligations = fail-CI-active; conditional_validation_obligations = mandatory only once the activation predicate is implemented; planned_validator_records = a separate report-only planned-coverage status (and is NOT in the parsed ReconstructContractRegistry type, so the planned tier needs a separate raw-YAML read or a loader extension).

Register as a net-NEW guard, following the exact G8/G9 contract: a pure exported evaluate*()->string[] comparator with a co-located self-test, a thin main() with the direct-invoke guard, a new `check:*` npm script, and a new GUARDS[] entry in scripts/check-invariant-drift.ts mapped to an INV id. Reuse listDelta/duplicateIds/setDiff and the violation()+validation_status artifact shape from registry-verification-validation.ts; do NOT introduce a parallel coverage machine.

Reuse the existing failure vocabulary verbatim — missing_required_coverage (obligation with no recorded assertion), duplicate_id, conflicting_state / registry_claim_mismatch (recorded id not mapping to a current registry obligation per onto issue-001's reverse-validation). Net-new obligation/failure concepts = 0 (design §4 concept-economy).

The M1 helpers (validateMaturationBaseline:696, validateActionabilityMatrix:1071) are the already-live named enforcers for the two P1 obligations and must be wired as the recorded enforcers; their current validation_results is a fixed 2-value array, so the recording channel must be ADDED to them (and to every other active validator) — coverage is only meaningful once recording is universal across the active tier.

There is no registry-driven validator dispatcher — validators are called per-stage in run.ts. So the 'CI fixture executes each validator path' alternative has no runner to reuse and must be built; the per-validator validate*/write*ValidationArtifact functions are the execution targets. Whichever dynamic-proof route is chosen, the execution substrate is invented, not reused.

The gate must also reverse-validate recorded asserted_obligation_ids back against the current registry/tier/owner/activation rules (onto self-review issue-001 in .onto/review/20260619-fa98af28): a recorded id that no longer corresponds to an active registry obligation is itself drift, not silently accepted.
bounding-and-prior-deferral: DYNAMIC PROOF ONLY: a static obligation_id->assertion_handle map is forbidden (it re-creates 'declared != wired'). The proof must be that validators RECORD the obligation ids they actually asserted (asserted_obligation_ids in the validation artifact, or a CI fixture that drives each validator path and captures invoked handles); the gate fails CI when an in-scope ACTIVE obligation has no recorded assertion. Evidence: design §3 G(a) (20260619-...-design.md:75); recording field absent today (asserted_obligation_ids = 0 hits in src/).

TIER-SCOPED, NOT ALL-297-AT-ONCE: scope = validator_records.validation_obligations (40 active validators, 267 flat) as mandatory-active; conditional_validation_obligations (5) mandatory only once each activation_condition predicate is implemented; planned_validator_records (8 validators, 25 obligations) as a separate planned-coverage STATUS, never forced active. The gate must distinguish these tiers so it is neither vacuous (gating nothing) nor a 297-line chore (gating everything before enforcers exist).

FIRST SLICE MUST BE THE M1-ENFORCED TRIO (19 obligations): start with only maturation-baseline-validator (6), baseline-actionability-matrix-validator (6), actionability-matrix-validator (7) — the validators whose obligations M1 (validateMaturationBaseline:696 / validateActionabilityMatrix:1071) already enforce at runtime. This delivers the P1 silent-defect-as-build-error value on an existing substrate with a ~19-id blast radius; obligations on validators with no enforcer yet must be declared 'planned coverage', not silently passed.

NON-VACUOUS COMPLETENESS: mirror the G9 static source-region sweep (check-final-output-sections-parity.ts:17-21) — the gate must detect a NEWLY ADDED active in-scope obligation that has no recorded assertion (coverage over the obligation SET, not spot-checks of known ids), so that adding an obligation to the YAML without an enforcer fails CI. It must not be foolable by an obligation that is declared-covered but whose recording is a coarse pass/fail token.

RECORDING SUBSTRATE IS PER-VALIDATOR CODE, NOT ONE GATE: validation_results: string[] exists on 42 validation-artifact interfaces but today carries only a coarse '<name>_valid'/'<name>_invalid' token (maturation-validation.ts:921-923). G(a) must add structured asserted_obligation_ids emission to each in-scope validator (a typed field + builder code change across artifact-types.ts + the validator functions), threaded through write-fns/run.ts call sites — this is the real surface cost the deferral named; bound it by tier.

HASH-SAFE / NO REUSE-HASH ROTATION: any new validation-artifact field G(a) adds must NOT rotate the governing-snapshot/reuse hash (the #108 lesson). asserted_obligation_ids is a validation OUTPUT (not part of the validator_records snapshot family), so it should be naturally excluded, but the G(a) design must verify governing-snapshot.test + reuse-provenance tests stay green, mirroring the projectValidatorRecordSnapshotFields allow-list discipline from #108.

REGISTER AS A NEW GUARD IN check-invariant-drift.ts WITH A DELIBERATE INV: add a {guard, invariants, command} entry that process.exit(1) on uncovered active obligations (G8/G9 precedent at check-invariant-drift.ts:30-71). Do NOT reuse INV-SCHEMA-1 unreflectively — G(a) is enforcement-coverage, not schema-shape; decide between a new INV (e.g. INV-OBLIGATION-COVERAGE-1, INVARIANT-CHANGE-marked) and an existing one, since no current invariant expresses 'declared obligation -> live recorded enforcer'.

CONCEPT ECONOMY: reuse the existing failure/recording vocabulary (validation_results, the missing_required_coverage / conflicting_state codes) and the loader fields already preserved by #108; introduce at most one new field concept (asserted_obligation_ids) plus one guard script + one INV. Net-new obligation CONCEPTS must be 0 — G(a) wires existing declared obligations, it does not invent new ones.
